Dispositions: publish | withhold | user_pending | publish_after. The publish set is exactly `disposition == publish`; everything else stays out of the public tree (a user_pending row is withheld-for-now, not withheld-forever).
_derived_from: git ls-files at HEAD -- NOT from docs/fork-inventory.md sec 3, which this file supersedes. The inventory was measured 2026-09-12 against a four-milestone-older tree and enumerated by hand; enumerating from it again was the named risk on the F5A tracker item. This is the tools/data/libref_asset_dispositions.json (F4G) precedent applied to the whole tree.

It is NOT the same question as KEEP-vs-ARCHIVE, which is F5G's (is this tool still used?). Where the two could disagree, this ledger takes the publish call and F5G refines within `tools/`; F5G's disposition file must not contradict a row here without saying so.

_public_tree_marker.why: fork F5M: HOW A TOOL TELLS THE PRIVATE WORKING TREE FROM THE CUT'S OUTPUT, declared here rather than inferred at each call site. A tree is the CUT'S OUTPUT when the named rule owns ZERO tracked paths. That rule is the research repo itself -- notes/, session_reports/, tasks/, tracker/, .claude/, report/ and the four root process documents -- so a private checkout always carries some of it and the public cut never carries any of it. WHY NOT THE OBVIOUS TEST ('no tracked path is non-published'): that answer is destroyed by the very defect the public check exists to catch. One leaked baseline PNG would make a public clone read as private, the public arms would never run, and the leak would go unreported. Keying on ONE rule that a leak elsewhere cannot touch keeps the detector honest -- and a leak of THIS rule's own files is still caught, because the private arms then run against a tree where every other withhold rule matches nothing, which is their dead-rule failure. Either way it is RED, which is the only property that matters. Used by check_publishable --public and by lint_repo, which chooses the publish-ledger rows by tree rather than by its --ci flag (--ci runs on the private repo too).

_rule_semantics: Rules are evaluated IN ORDER; the FIRST rule whose glob set matches a path owns it. So specific rows precede the subtree rows they carve out of. `globs` are fnmatch patterns over the forward-slash repo-relative path.

_closure_exception_semantics: A row here declares a KNOWN edge from a published source into a path the public tree does not carry. `source` and `needs` are globs (or lists of globs). A declared row suppresses the failure AND MUST STILL REPRODUCE: when the edge is gone, the row goes stale and the check FAILS until it is deleted. That is what stops this list from becoming the place violations go to be forgotten. Only edges into WITHHOLD targets can fail in the first place -- an edge into a user_pending/publish_after target is reported as CONDITIONAL, grouped by the question it waits on, because it is a measurement of what an answer costs and not a defect.
